about: Authored quick-round questions only. Difficulty is an editorial estimate, not measured accuracy. IDs and answer meanings are immutable once deployed: retire a flawed ID and add a new one. Ranked schedules and the full assessment use their existing banks.

items.prompt: Mercury is closest to the Sun. Which planet has the hotter surface?
items.explanation: Venus wins: its thick atmosphere traps heat. Being closer to the Sun is not enough to make Mercury hotter.

items.prompt: An ice cube floats in water. What makes that possible?
options: Ice is less dense than liquid water
Ice is denser than liquid water
items.explanation: Water expands as it freezes, so the same mass takes up more space. That lower density lets ordinary ice float.

items.prompt: A sound has to travel one kilometre. Where does it arrive sooner?
items.explanation: Sound travels about 1,500 m/s in seawater versus roughly 340 m/s in air. Water carries the vibration much faster.

items.prompt: What makes the Moon look like a crescent on an ordinary night?
options: We see only part of its sunlit half
Earth's shadow covers most of it
items.explanation: The Moon's phases come from our changing view of its sunlit half. Earth's shadow causes a lunar eclipse, not the monthly phases.

items.prompt: Two solid cubes are the same size: one gold, one lead. Which weighs more?
items.explanation: Gold is denser: about 19.3 g/cm³ versus 11.3 for lead. Lead feels heavy until you give gold the same volume.

items.prompt: Which visible light has the longer wavelength?
items.explanation: Red sits at the long-wavelength end of visible light; blue sits nearer the short-wavelength end. Bluer does not mean longer.

items.prompt: How many hearts does an octopus have?
items.explanation: Two hearts send blood to the gills. A third sends it around the body. Eight arms, three hearts.

items.prompt: Which living animal is more closely related to a whale?
items.explanation: Hippos are whales' closest living relatives. A shared swimming lifestyle makes seals look like the better guess.

items.prompt: Whose typical body cell has more chromosomes?
items.explanation: Chimpanzees have 48; humans have 46. Human chromosome 2 formed from the fusion of two ancestral chromosomes.

items.prompt: In 'small intestine' and 'large intestine', what does 'large' mainly describe?
items.explanation: The large intestine is wider. The small intestine is actually the longer one, despite its name.

items.prompt: A bat uses echolocation. Does that mean it cannot see?
items.explanation: Bats have working eyes. Echolocation adds information about their surroundings; it does not replace vision because they are blind.

items.prompt: Under all that pale fur, what colour is a polar bear's skin?
items.explanation: The skin is black. The pale appearance comes from the fur, so the colour you see is not the colour underneath.

items.prompt: Why is it summer in Australia when it is winter in Europe?
options: Earth's distance from the Sun changes
items.explanation: The hemispheres tilt toward the Sun at opposite times of year. A change in Earth's distance would affect both hemispheres together.

items.prompt: Which ocean covers more area?
items.explanation: The Pacific is the largest ocean basin. NOAA notes that all the continents could fit inside it.

items.prompt: Much of Antarctica is a desert. What qualifies it?
items.explanation: Deserts are defined by dryness, not heat. Antarctica's interior receives very little snowfall despite all the ice already there.

items.prompt: You stand at the North Pole in June. On a clear day, does the Sun set?
options: No, it stays above the horizon
items.explanation: The North Pole tilts toward the Sun during northern summer. Earth keeps spinning, but the pole stays on the sunlit side.

items.prompt: Which summit is farther from the centre of Earth?
items.explanation: Everest is higher above sea level. Chimborazo is nearer the equator, where Earth's bulge puts its summit farther from the centre.

items.prompt: Put Everest in the ocean with its base at Challenger Deep. Would its summit reach the surface?
options: No, it would still be underwater
items.explanation: Challenger Deep is roughly 11 km below the surface; Everest rises about 8.85 km above sea level. There would still be about 2 km of water overhead.

items.prompt: Before Mario, what did Nintendo originally make?
items.explanation: Nintendo began making hanafuda playing cards in Kyoto in 1889. Video games came much later.

items.prompt: Before streaming, which format did Netflix rent by mail?
items.explanation: Netflix launched its online DVD rental store in 1998. The red envelope came before the streaming queue.

items.prompt: LEGO started making toys in 1932. What were those early toys mainly made of?
items.explanation: Ole Kirk Kristiansen's early toys were wooden, including cars and aeroplanes. The plastic brick was a later chapter.

items.prompt: Where was Tetris created?
items.explanation: Alexey Pajitnov created Tetris in Moscow in 1984 on an Electronika 60 computer. Its later Nintendo success can make Tokyo feel like the obvious answer.

items.prompt: The Oscar statuette design introduced in 2016 is made from what?
items.explanation: The Academy returned to a cast-bronze statuette finished in 24-karat gold. The gold is the finish, not the whole statue.

items.prompt: Your queen is still on the chessboard. Can you promote a pawn to a second queen?
items.explanation: Promotion is not limited to pieces that have been captured. A pawn reaching the last rank can become another queen.

items.prompt: Bubble Wrap began as an attempt to make what?
items.explanation: The inventors first tried to sell it as textured wallpaper. Protecting packages turned out to be the better use.

items.prompt: QR codes were originally developed for which setting?
items.explanation: DENSO WAVE released the QR code in 1994. The auto industry used it to track production and logistics long before phone menus.

items.prompt: What inspired the hooks in VELCRO fasteners?
options: Burrs caught in fur and fabric
items.explanation: George de Mestral examined clinging burrs and found tiny hooks. He copied that hook-and-loop mechanism into a reusable fastener.

items.prompt: What is the dark writing material in an ordinary 'lead' pencil?
items.explanation: The core uses graphite, usually mixed with clay. The everyday name 'pencil lead' does not describe the metal lead.

items.prompt: A thick potato is in a microwave. Is it cooked from the inside out?
options: No, heat also has to conduct inward
items.explanation: Microwaves penetrate only so far into thick food. The outer layers absorb energy, and heat conducts toward the centre.

items.prompt: Botanically, the potato you eat is a swollen what?
items.explanation: A potato is a stem tuber. Its 'eyes' are buds that can grow new shoots, a clue to what it really is.

items.prompt: A fair coin lands heads five times in independent flips. Chance of tails next?
items.explanation: The coin has no memory. With independent fair flips, the next result is still 50–50; tails is not 'due'.

items.prompt: A $100 price rises 20%, then falls 20%. Where does it end?
items.explanation: $100 × 1.20 = $120, then $120 × 0.80 = $96. The second percentage applies to a different starting amount.

items.prompt: For 23 independent, uniformly distributed birthdays on 365 days, is the chance of a shared birthday above 50%?
items.explanation: It is about 50.7%. There are 253 pairs of people, so there are many more chances for a match than 23 might suggest.

items.prompt: You drive 60 miles at 30 mph, then 60 miles at 60 mph. Average speed for the whole trip?
items.explanation: The trip takes 2 hours plus 1 hour. That's 120 miles in 3 hours: 40 mph. You spend more time at the slower speed.

items.prompt: Roll two independent fair six-sided dice. Which total is more likely?
items.explanation: Six ordered outcomes make 7; only (6, 6) makes 12. That is 6 chances in 36 versus 1 in 36.

items.prompt: A bat and ball cost $1.10 together. The bat costs $1 more than the ball. Ball's price?
items.explanation: At 5 cents for the ball, the bat is $1.05 and the total is $1.10. A 10-cent ball would make the total $1.20.

items.prompt: AlphaGo's famous match against Lee Sedol was played in which game?
items.explanation: Lee Sedol faced AlphaGo at Go in 2016. AlphaZero later tackled chess, shogi and Go.

items.prompt: Why did OpenAI initially withhold the full GPT-2 model in 2019?
options: It could not generate text yet
items.explanation: OpenAI released a smaller model first while studying misuse risks. The full 1.5-billion-parameter model came later that year.

items.prompt: In a language model, is one token always one whole word?
options: No, it can be part of a word
Yes, one word always equals one token
items.explanation: Tokens can be word pieces, whole words, punctuation or characters. A word count is not a reliable token count.

items.prompt: ImageNet was built around which kind of data?
items.explanation: ImageNet organises images into a hierarchy of concepts. Its image-recognition challenge helped make deep learning famous.

items.prompt: What powered the original 1966 ELIZA chatbot?
options: Rules that matched and rearranged text
items.explanation: ELIZA used keyword rules and response templates. Convincing conversation existed long before today's large language models.

items.prompt: The original Transformer replaced recurrence with what main mechanism?
items.explanation: The 2017 paper built the Transformer around attention, removing recurrent and convolutional layers from that architecture.

items.prompt: A classifier assigns 90% confidence. Does that number alone prove it is right 90% of the time?
items.explanation: A score is not a guarantee of calibration. A model can be confident more often than it is correct, just like a player here.

items.prompt: For the same number of weights, which needs less raw storage, ignoring overhead?
items.explanation: Four bits per weight is one quarter of sixteen. Real memory use also includes scales, activations and other overhead.

items.prompt: A RAG assistant needs today's policy document. What is the retrieval step for?
options: Finding relevant text to supply to the model
items.explanation: Retrieval supplies outside information for generation. Fetching a document is different from updating the model's learned weights.

items.prompt: During BERT's masked-word pretraining, which context can help fill a blank?
items.explanation: BERT was designed to learn from left and right context together. The 'B' stands for bidirectional.

items.prompt: How did AlphaZero learn game strategy, given the rules?
options: A database of human expert games
items.explanation: AlphaZero trained by playing against itself. Unlike the original AlphaGo, it did not need human game records to learn its strategy.

items.prompt: Which was published first?
items.explanation: The Transformer paper appeared in 2017; GPT-3's paper appeared in 2020. GPT-3 built on the Transformer family.

items.prompt: The largest model in the original GPT-3 paper had how many parameters?
items.explanation: The paper's largest GPT-3 model had 175 billion parameters. The decimal point changes the answer by a factor of ten.

items.prompt: In a standard denoising diffusion model, how is a new image generated?
options: By retrieving an unchanged training image
items.explanation: The model learns a reverse process that turns noise into an image step by step. It is not simply an image-search engine.

items.prompt: In neural-network training, what does 'dropout' mean?
items.explanation: Dropout randomly omits units during training to reduce overfitting. It is not the same operation as permanently pruning a network.

items.prompt: GPT-3 gets a few worked examples in its prompt, with no training step. What changes?
items.explanation: The original few-shot setup supplied examples as text, with no gradient updates. The model used a new context, not newly trained weights.

items.prompt: Only 1% of emails are spam. A filter labels every email 'not spam'. Its accuracy?
items.explanation: It gets the 99% non-spam messages right while catching zero spam. High accuracy can hide complete failure on the class you care about.

items.prompt: A filter flags 100 emails as spam; 20 really are spam. Its precision?
items.explanation: Precision asks how many positive predictions were correct: 20 divided by 100. It is not the fraction of all spam caught.

items.prompt: Did the original GPT-4 technical report disclose its parameter count?
items.explanation: The report withheld model-size and architecture details. A widely repeated parameter count is not the same as a number disclosed in that report.

items.prompt: What task was the original Transformer paper mainly evaluated on?
items.explanation: Its main experiments translated English to German and French. Chatbots were not the original paper's benchmark.

items.prompt: For a two-token output: P(A)=0.6, P(B)=0.4; best continuations have P(x|A)=0.5, P(y|B)=0.9. Which sequence is likelier?
items.explanation: P(Ax)=0.6×0.5=0.30; P(By)=0.4×0.9=0.36. Taking the most likely first token need not give the most likely whole sequence.

items.prompt: In top-p (nucleus) sampling, does p set a fixed number of candidate tokens?
items.explanation: The nucleus grows or shrinks with the probability distribution. Top-k fixes a token count; top-p uses cumulative probability.

items.prompt: A perfectly calibrated model makes many 70%-confidence predictions. Roughly how many should be right?
items.explanation: Calibration means the confidence matches the long-run success rate. Being well calibrated still allows mistakes.

items.prompt: In the original LoRA method, what gets trained?
items.explanation: LoRA freezes the pretrained weights and trains low-rank updates. Adapting a model does not always mean updating every original weight.

items.prompt: Someone yells "SIX..." and starts moving their palms up and down. Finish the brainrot.
items.explanation: Six-seven is the callout. The seesaw hand motion is part of the meme; no arithmetic required.

items.prompt: In the original "9 + 10" Vine, what does the kid answer? Not what your calculator says.
items.explanation: He answers 21. The actual sum is 19, which is exactly why the clip became a meme.

items.prompt: Damn, Daniel. Back at it again with the...
items.explanation: The viral clip keeps coming back to Daniel's white Vans. The shoes got their own internet career.

items.prompt: "Road work ahead?" Finish Drew Gooden's Vine.
options: No, it's on its lunch break
Uh, yeah, I sure hope it does
items.explanation: Gooden treats "work" as a verb: he hopes the road works. One sign, one joke, permanent brain storage.

items.prompt: A shark pulls up in Nike sneakers. Which brainrot creature just entered the chat?
items.explanation: Tralalero Tralala is associated with the sneaker-wearing shark. The crocodile has a very different transport situation.

items.prompt: Tung Tung Tung Sahur is outside. What is the wooden creature holding?
items.explanation: The familiar image shows a wooden creature carrying a bat or club. Somehow the wood has armed itself with more wood.

items.prompt: Ballerina Cappuccina has a ballet body. What is her head?
items.explanation: The character combines a ballet dancer with a cappuccino cup. Your coffee has choreography now.

items.prompt: Hands in pockets. Sweater. Zero stress. "Chill Guy" is drawn as what animal?
items.explanation: Phillip Banks' character is a brown dog with a human body, sweater, jeans and shoes. Extremely committed to the bit.

items.prompt: Your friend sends "the exam answers." The link opens Rick Astley singing. What just happened?
items.explanation: A rickroll disguises the video for Never Gonna Give You Up as the thing you actually wanted to open.

items.prompt: Three deadlines. Laptop crashing. You say "This is fine." What is happening around the original meme dog?
items.explanation: K.C. Green's dog sits in a burning room and insists things are fine. Very strong denial, very weak fire response.

items.prompt: You skip every lecture, fail the exam, and act shocked. Which reaction image fits that predictable result?
items.explanation: Surprised Pikachu is commonly paired with someone reacting in shock to a consequence they could have predicted.

items.prompt: A streamer loops canned reactions like a video-game background character. The joke is that they are acting like an...
items.explanation: NPC means non-player character. The meme borrows the idea of scripted, repetitive game-character behavior.

items.prompt: Who made "Doot Doot," the song behind the 6–7 meme?
items.explanation: The six-seven audio comes from Skrilla's Doot Doot. Basketball edits helped turn the lyric into an everywhere phrase.

items.prompt: Which creator launched the original Skibidi Toilet series?
items.explanation: DaFuq!?Boom! created the animated series about singing toilet heads and their increasingly elaborate battles.

items.prompt: Who is the comedian behind the viral "EMOTIONAL DAMAGE" shout?
items.explanation: Steven He delivered the line in a comedy sketch. The reaction clip then escaped into everybody else's videos.

items.prompt: Which game gave us the actual "Press F to pay respects" prompt?
items.explanation: The PC version of Advanced Warfare uses the prompt during a funeral scene. The internet kept the F.

items.prompt: The original side-eye Doge photo stars which actual dog?
items.explanation: Kabosu is the Shiba Inu in the iconic Doge photo. Balltze is the different dog associated with Cheems.

items.prompt: Which chain sold the purple Grimace Shake that TikTok turned into a horror-movie prop?
items.explanation: McDonald's released the purple shake for Grimace's birthday in 2023. The horror scenes were a user-made trend.

items.prompt: Tung Tung Tung Sahur gets grouped with Italian brainrot. Where did the character actually originate?
items.explanation: The meme originated with Indonesian creator @noxaasht and an Indonesian voice-over. "Italian brainrot" is not everyone's birthplace.

items.prompt: Bombardiro Crocodilo is a crocodile fused with what?
items.explanation: The original character is a crocodile-aircraft hybrid. The animal kingdom apparently has an air force.

items.prompt: Nyan Cat flies through space with a rainbow trail. Its torso is what snack?
items.explanation: Chris Torres' pixel cat has a Pop-Tart body. Toast is a different breakfast-based flight system.

items.prompt: In "Is this a pigeon?", what is the character actually pointing at?
items.explanation: The Fighbird character points at a butterfly and calls it a pigeon. Confidence: high. Bird identification: catastrophic.

items.prompt: One does not simply walk into...
items.explanation: Boromir says the line in The Fellowship of the Ring. The internet then applied it to every mildly difficult task.

items.prompt: Keep the original broken grammar: "All your base..."
items.explanation: The famous Zero Wing translation is "All your base are belong to us." Fixing the grammar breaks the reference.

items.prompt: The original Happy Cat request: "I can has..."
items.explanation: The Happy Cat image helped popularize "I Can Has Cheezburger?" and the deliberately mangled grammar of LOLcats.

items.prompt: Label a Distracted Boyfriend meme: the guy is you, the passing woman is one more quiz. Who gets labelled "my unfinished essay"?
items.explanation: The girlfriend represents the existing commitment; the passerby is the tempting distraction. Your essay knows what you did.

items.prompt: Someone puts a ridiculous take beside the biggest glowing Galaxy Brain. Does the format guarantee they think the take is smart?
options: No; the ranking is often ironic
Yes; the biggest brain is always sincere
items.explanation: Galaxy Brain often escalates toward absurdity. The increasingly cosmic brain can be the joke, not an endorsement.

items.prompt: Buy high, sell low, post the suited 3D head in front of a stock chart. Which caption completes the financial disaster?
items.explanation: Stonks uses Meme Man and a stock-market backdrop to joke about financial decisions, especially bad ones.

items.prompt: A handful of lines makes the chat say "Is this Loss?" Which webcomic published the original strip?
items.explanation: Tim Buckley published Loss in Ctrl+Alt+Del in 2008. Its four-panel composition became recognizable even as a few lines.

items.prompt: Before Hide the Pain Harold became internet-famous, what was András Arató's career?
items.explanation: Arató was an electrical engineer before his stock-photo smile became a reaction image.

items.prompt: Big Chungus looks like internet nonsense. Which actual cartoon supplied the Bugs Bunny frame?
items.explanation: Bugs briefly imitates a portly Elmer Fudd in Wabbit Twouble. The frame is decades older than the meme.

items.prompt: Keyboard Cat has had successors. Name the cat in the original footage.
items.explanation: Fatso appears in Charlie Schmidt's original footage. Bento was a later Keyboard Cat, not the original.

items.prompt: The house behind Disaster Girl really was burning. What was going on?
items.explanation: The photo was taken during a controlled fire for firefighter training in North Carolina. The meme's sinister story is invented.

items.prompt: The white cat opposite the yelling Real Housewife has a name. Who is it?
items.explanation: Smudge is the cat sitting behind a plate of vegetables. The cat photo and reality-show frame were separate images.

items.prompt: Why can "|  ||  ||  |_" work as a Loss meme without a single face?
options: The lines echo the figures in its four panels
It spells LOSS in Morse code
items.explanation: The line groups preserve the original comic's character arrangement, including the lying figure in the last panel.

items.prompt: The famous 2011 Nyan Cat video uses a cover. Which voice sings that version?
items.explanation: Daniwell-P's song was originally written for Hatsune Miku, but the famous Nyan Cat video uses a Momone Momo cover.

items.prompt: Why did LaMelo Ball slot so neatly into the original 6–7 edits?
items.explanation: The edits hook the six-seven lyric to a description of Ball's height. The 67 is not his jersey number.

items.prompt: "Is this a pigeon?" looks like a subtitle fail. In the original scene, which explanation is right?
options: The subtitles mistranslate a correct answer
The character really misidentifies the butterfly
items.explanation: The mistake belongs to the character learning about Earth's wildlife. It is not a translator turning a correct identification into nonsense.

items.prompt: A friend says the original Skibidi Toilet videos were generated from AI text prompts. What actually made them?
items.explanation: The original series uses Source Filmmaker. Surreal toilet lore and AI-generated footage are not the same thing.

items.prompt: An early rickroll promised footage of a hotly anticipated GTA game. Which one was the bait in the documented 2007 story?
items.explanation: The early account describes a link disguised as a GTA IV preview. The surprise destination was Rick Astley.

items.prompt: One decree, three scripts. What did the Rosetta Stone help scholars decipher?
items.explanation: Its Greek text gave scholars a way into the Egyptian writing on the same stone.

items.prompt: The Terracotta Army was buried to serve a ruler of which empire?
items.explanation: The soldiers belong to the tomb complex of Qin Shi Huang, China's first emperor.

items.prompt: Who built Machu Picchu in the Andes?
items.explanation: Machu Picchu was an Inca site built in the fifteenth century, in what is now Peru.

items.prompt: How do Great Zimbabwe's famous stone walls stay together?
items.explanation: The walls use dry-stone masonry: fitted stones rather than mortar.

items.prompt: Angkor's temples were at the heart of which empire?
items.explanation: Angkor preserves successive Khmer capitals in present-day Cambodia.

items.prompt: You join the Underground Railroad in the United States. What are you helping people do?
items.explanation: It was a network of routes, people, and safe places that aided escape from slavery.

items.prompt: In 1893, New Zealand became the first self-governing country where all adult women could ___.
items.explanation: The 1893 law extended parliamentary voting rights to women; it did not appoint them to office.

items.prompt: Who took the first human step onto the Moon during Apollo 11?
items.explanation: Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed. Collins remained in lunar orbit.

items.prompt: The Sutton Hoo ship burial belonged to which culture?
items.explanation: The early medieval burial in England is a major source of Anglo-Saxon objects.

items.prompt: Mansa Musa, famous for his gold-rich pilgrimage, ruled which empire?
items.explanation: Mansa Musa ruled Mali, which was connected to trans-Saharan gold trade.

items.prompt: A merchant says the Silk Roads carried only silk. Is that accurate?
options: No, many goods and ideas also travelled
items.explanation: The name covers trade networks that also moved beliefs, technologies, and other goods.

items.prompt: How were Lalibela's most famous churches made?
options: Cast as single pieces of bronze
items.explanation: The Ethiopian churches were cut into living rock rather than assembled from bronze.

items.prompt: Which ancient trading city is famous for buildings cut into rose-coloured rock?
items.explanation: Petra, in present-day Jordan, combines rock-cut buildings with constructed ones.

items.prompt: The US Declaration of Independence was adopted in ___.
items.explanation: Congress adopted the Declaration on July 4, 1776.

items.prompt: Gunpowder's early development is associated with which place?
items.explanation: Gunpowder developed in China before spreading elsewhere.

items.prompt: Norse buildings at L'Anse aux Meadows are evidence of a settlement in which place?
items.explanation: The site preserves evidence of Norse settlement in North America around the eleventh century.

items.prompt: The Cyrus Cylinder is made of what?
items.explanation: The clay cylinder carries a cuneiform inscription from ancient Babylon.

items.prompt: The giant moai statues belong to the history of ___.
items.explanation: The Rapa Nui people created the island's monumental statues and ceremonial platforms.

items.prompt: An 1840 document signed by Māori chiefs and representatives of the British Crown is the Treaty of ___.
items.explanation: The Treaty of Waitangi is central to New Zealand's history.

items.prompt: Who rebelled at Australia's Eureka Stockade in 1854?
items.explanation: Miners at Ballarat protested the colonial administration of the goldfields.

items.prompt: Magna Carta is famous for establishing that a king ___.
items.explanation: The 1215 charter limited royal power, though it was not a modern universal-rights document.

items.prompt: Toussaint Louverture is associated with which revolution?
items.explanation: Louverture was a major leader in the revolution against slavery and colonial rule in Saint-Domingue.

items.prompt: Spanish Mexico City was built over the ruins of which city?
items.explanation: The Spanish colonial city was constructed on the site of the Aztec capital.

items.prompt: The historic Kingdom of Benin was mainly in what is now which country?
items.explanation: Despite the shared name, the kingdom was in present-day southern Nigeria.

items.prompt: Which material was one of ancient China's famous four inventions?
items.explanation: Paper, printing, the compass, and gunpowder are traditionally grouped as the four great inventions.

items.prompt: You visit Aztec Ruins National Monument in New Mexico. Who actually built its ancient structures?
items.explanation: The site's name is misleading: it preserves Ancestral Pueblo architecture.

items.prompt: Timbuktu's historical reputation includes being a centre of ___.
items.explanation: Its mosques and learning centres connected scholarship with Saharan trade.

items.prompt: The emperor Akbar sponsored major illustrated manuscripts in which empire?
items.explanation: Akbar's court supported an imperial workshop where different artistic traditions met.

items.prompt: The Rosetta Stone was rediscovered in 1799 by soldiers from which country?
items.explanation: French soldiers found it near Rashid, also called Rosetta, in Egypt.

items.prompt: The principal drafter of the US Declaration of Independence was ___.
items.explanation: Jefferson prepared the draft for a committee; Congress then debated and edited it.

items.prompt: A label says the Rosetta Stone has three scripts, so it must have three languages. What is wrong?
options: It has two languages: Egyptian and Greek
items.explanation: Hieroglyphic and demotic are both used for Egyptian; the third script writes Greek.

items.prompt: Besides temples, what helped Angkor support a large urban landscape?
items.explanation: Angkor's archaeological remains include basins, dykes, reservoirs, and canals.

items.prompt: What valuable commodity travelled south across the Sahara in exchange for gold?
items.explanation: Saharan salt and West African gold were central goods in these trading networks.

items.prompt: Lalibela's rock-hewn churches belong to which religious tradition?
items.explanation: The site remains a centre of Ethiopian Christian pilgrimage and worship.

items.prompt: During the Apollo 11 landing, Michael Collins ___.
options: Orbited the Moon in the command module
items.explanation: Collins piloted Columbia while Armstrong and Aldrin descended in Eagle.

items.prompt: Mughal painting under Akbar drew on which combination?
items.explanation: Artists brought Persian training and Indian approaches into the imperial workshop.

items.prompt: Why can simply comparing signatures fail to settle debates about the Treaty of Waitangi?
options: Its English and Māori texts differ in meaning
Its two texts are word-for-word identical
items.explanation: Differences between the texts are central to disagreements about what was agreed.

items.prompt: Why is it misleading to say everyone signed the Declaration on July 4, 1776?
options: Adoption and the main signing were on different dates
items.explanation: Congress adopted it on July 4; most delegates signed the engrossed copy on August 2.

items.prompt: At L'Anse aux Meadows, which building materials fit the archaeological evidence?
items.explanation: The Norse settlement includes turf-walled, timber-framed structures.

items.prompt: Did Magna Carta introduce equal voting rights for every adult in 1215?
items.explanation: Its immediate context was a dispute between King John and barons, not universal suffrage.

items.prompt: Zhang Qian's Han-era journeys into Central Asia began as what kind of mission?
items.explanation: The Han envoy's travels helped expand knowledge and contacts along routes later called Silk Roads.

items.prompt: Xochimilco preserves canals and chinampas: ___.
options: Raised agricultural plots in a wetland system
items.explanation: Chinampas were cultivated plots built in the shallow lake environment around Mexico City.

items.prompt: A museum label calls a Benin object a 'bronze'. Must its metal actually be bronze?
options: No; many such objects are brass
Yes; the label guarantees the alloy
items.explanation: The collective name Benin Bronzes includes many works made from brass.

items.prompt: Early gunpowder rockets moved mainly because ___.
items.explanation: Gas escaping from the rocket produced thrust.

items.prompt: The Eureka rebels' flag prominently featured which constellation?
items.explanation: The Southern Cross flag became an enduring symbol associated with the rebellion.

items.prompt: The Cyrus Cylinder's inscription is written in which writing system?
items.explanation: Its wedge-shaped signs record a Babylonian royal inscription.

items.prompt: On Rapa Nui, moai statues are associated with ceremonial platforms called ___.
items.explanation: Ahu are monumental ceremonial structures in the island's cultural landscape.

items.prompt: Could Toussaint Louverture have attended Haiti's declaration of independence in 1804?
items.explanation: Louverture died in French captivity before independence was proclaimed.

items.prompt: Which campaigner is closely associated with New Zealand's women's suffrage petitions?
items.explanation: Sheppard was a leading organiser of the campaign that helped win voting rights in 1893.

items.prompt: How did King John authenticate Magna Carta?
items.explanation: Royal documents were authenticated with a seal; 'signed Magna Carta' is misleading shorthand.

items.prompt: On the Rosetta Stone, which script sits alongside hieroglyphic and Greek?
items.explanation: Demotic was another script for the Egyptian language.

items.prompt: Which is the safer description of the Cyrus Cylinder in its own historical setting?
options: A modern bill granting universal equal rights
A royal inscription legitimising a conquest
items.explanation: It presents Cyrus's rule and restoration policies through a Babylonian royal tradition.

items.prompt: Qin Shi Huang unified China in ___.
items.explanation: The Qin unification belongs to the third century BCE, centuries before 221 CE.

items.prompt: How did Petra's inhabitants manage water in an arid setting?
options: A permanent glacier in the city centre
items.explanation: The Nabataeans engineered water collection, storage, and distribution systems.

items.prompt: Many Benin brass plaques were originally associated with what setting?
items.explanation: The plaques formed part of the palace's art and recorded court life and history.

items.prompt: Many Benin objects entered British collections after which event?
items.explanation: British forces looted Benin City in 1897; many objects were dispersed internationally.

items.prompt: A history describes Timbuktu only as an isolated desert outpost. What major role does it miss?
options: A centre of scholarship and trade
items.explanation: Its mosques and scholarly institutions were linked to trans-Saharan networks.

items.prompt: Akbar's manuscript workshop brought together artists from which backgrounds?
items.explanation: Mughal court production brought artists with different backgrounds into shared projects.

items.prompt: Jefferson drafted the Declaration as part of a committee of ___.
items.explanation: The committee included Jefferson, Adams, Franklin, Sherman, and Livingston.

items.prompt: Which happened first in 1776?
options: Most delegates signed its engrossed copy
items.explanation: Adoption was July 4; the main signing of the engrossed copy was August 2.

items.prompt: What makes the date of New Zealand's Matariki public holiday shift each year?
options: Its link to a particular lunar period
Its link to the March equinox
items.explanation: The holiday falls near the Tangaroa lunar period in Pipiri, so its Gregorian date changes.

items.prompt: UNESCO associates the builders of Great Zimbabwe with which people?
items.explanation: The site is evidence of a major indigenous southern African civilisation.

items.prompt: A guide uses 'Aztec Ruins' to prove that the Aztec capital was in New Mexico. What is the problem?
options: The monument's name misidentifies its builders
The ruins are entirely modern replicas
items.explanation: The monument preserves Ancestral Pueblo structures, not the Aztec capital.

items.prompt: The Bayon temple is part of which historic complex?
items.explanation: Bayon stands at Angkor Thom within the Angkor landscape in Cambodia.

items.prompt: L'Anse aux Meadows connects medieval North America with which seafaring tradition?
items.explanation: Its buildings and artefacts provide evidence of a Norse settlement.

items.prompt: The first Māori King, selected in 1858, was ___.
items.explanation: Te Wherowhero became the first Māori King; he had not signed the Treaty of Waitangi.

items.prompt: Who became the leader of the Eureka miners?
items.explanation: Lalor, an Irish miner, led the protesters at Ballarat in 1854.

items.prompt: You need the spacecraft that actually landed Armstrong and Aldrin. Which name belongs on the label?
items.explanation: Eagle was the lunar module. Columbia was the command module that stayed in orbit.

items.prompt: Why could the Underground Railroad operate without railway tracks?
options: It relied on people, routes, and safe places
It was a tunnel running under the Atlantic
items.explanation: The name was a metaphor for a network aiding escape from slavery.

items.prompt: The historical Sahelian empires connected which two broad zones through trade?
options: The Sahara and lands to its south
items.explanation: Their position helped link Saharan routes with regions producing goods such as gold.

items.prompt: Was 'Silk Road' the name used by all ancient traders for one official highway?
options: No; the term was coined much later
Yes; it was a single ancient road name
items.explanation: The modern term dates to the nineteenth century and describes many routes.

items.prompt: Petra's great trading city is particularly associated with the ___.
items.explanation: The Nabataeans developed Petra as a trading centre linking several regions.

items.prompt: How many rock-hewn churches make up UNESCO's Lalibela property?
items.explanation: The listed site comprises eleven medieval monolithic and rock-hewn churches.

items.prompt: Which landscape best fits the historic setting of Machu Picchu?
options: A low coastal desert in Egypt
items.explanation: The Inca site sits in a dramatic mountain landscape in Peru.

items.prompt: Which Chinese invention made direction-finding less dependent on seeing the Sun or stars?
items.explanation: A magnetic compass provides a direction reference even when celestial bodies are hidden.

items.prompt: The famous Sutton Hoo helmet is evidence of what?
items.explanation: The helmet comes from an Anglo-Saxon ship burial with richly worked objects.

items.prompt: Which royal name on the Rosetta Stone helped early decipherment work?
items.explanation: The repeated royal name Ptolemy was an important clue for Thomas Young and other scholars.

items.prompt: A museum labels the 1215 Magna Carta as a bargain involving which English king?
items.explanation: The charter arose from the conflict between King John and his barons.

items.prompt: Mexico City's colonial core began to take shape under Spanish rule in which century?
items.explanation: The Spanish built the colonial city on Tenochtitlan's site during the sixteenth century.

items.prompt: The monumental culture that produced Rapa Nui's moai was ___.
items.explanation: Rapa Nui's people developed the island's distinctive monumental tradition within Polynesia.

items.prompt: Which writing system is used for Korean?
items.explanation: Hangul writes Korean using letters arranged in syllable blocks.

items.prompt: Which is a language isolate, with no established living relatives?
items.explanation: Basque is classified as an isolate. English belongs to the Germanic family.

items.prompt: Two Deaf people meet from different countries. Can you assume they share the same sign language?
items.explanation: There is no single universal sign language; different communities use different languages.

items.prompt: Touch your throat while saying 'zzzz' then 'ssss'. What usually changes?
items.explanation: The vocal folds vibrate for voiced /z/ but not for voiceless /s/.

items.prompt: In 'unhappy', the part 'un-' is a ___.
items.explanation: A prefix comes before its base; a suffix follows it.

items.prompt: A line of ordinary Arabic text is read mainly in which direction?
items.explanation: Arabic letters run right to left; numbers within the text can run the other way.

items.prompt: You find an undated note saying 'I'll come tomorrow.' What is missing if you want the exact day?
items.explanation: Words such as tomorrow depend on the time of the utterance.

items.prompt: Which is a compound made from two roots?
items.explanation: Toothbrush combines tooth and brush. Walked adds an inflection to walk.

items.prompt: Hum 'mmm' with your mouth closed. Where does most of the air escape?
items.explanation: For nasal consonants such as /m/, air can flow through the nose.

items.prompt: Despite its many French loanwords, English belongs to which branch?
items.explanation: A language's family follows historical descent, not just which words it has borrowed.

items.prompt: In 'The fox chased the hen', the basic order is ___.
items.explanation: The fox is the subject, chased the verb, and the hen the object.

items.prompt: Braille is best described as what?
items.explanation: Raised-dot patterns can be used to write different languages.

items.prompt: At dinner, someone says 'Can you pass the salt?' What are they usually doing?
items.explanation: What an utterance does in context can go beyond its literal question form.

items.prompt: Which pair differs by just one speech sound in standard English?
items.explanation: Pat and bat form a minimal pair: changing one sound changes the word.

items.prompt: A Korean Hangul block may look like one symbol. How is it normally built?
options: From letters arranged into a syllable
From a separate picture for each word
items.explanation: Hangul combines consonant and vowel letters spatially into syllable blocks.

items.prompt: The '-s' in 'cats' mainly tells you ___.
options: The cats are in the past
There is more than one cat
items.explanation: This is plural inflection on a noun, not past-tense marking.

items.prompt: Finnish belongs to which language family?
items.explanation: Finnish is Uralic, as are Estonian and Hungarian.

items.prompt: In a tone language, changing pitch on the same syllable can do what?
options: Only change how loudly it is spoken
items.explanation: Lexical tone uses pitch contrasts to distinguish words.

items.prompt: Which word gives a position in a sequence rather than a quantity?
items.explanation: Third is ordinal; three is cardinal.

items.prompt: American Sign Language has important historical links to which sign language?
items.explanation: French Sign Language contributed to ASL's development alongside local signing traditions.

items.prompt: Which script is commonly used to write Hindi?
items.explanation: Devanagari writes Hindi and several other languages.

items.prompt: A language makes a new form by repeating a word or part of it. What is this called?
items.explanation: Reduplication copies all or part of a form for a grammatical or word-building purpose.

items.prompt: An inclusive 'we' means the speaker and ___.
options: The person being addressed, possibly others too
Only people absent from the conversation
items.explanation: Inclusive we includes the addressee; exclusive we leaves the addressee out.

items.prompt: A book uses the Latin alphabet. Can you conclude that its language is Latin?
items.explanation: Many languages share the same script. A script and a language are different things.

items.prompt: Which sound requires both lips to come together?
items.explanation: The /p/ sound is bilabial: its closure is made with both lips.

items.prompt: Which word directly imitates a sound?
items.explanation: Onomatopoeic words imitate sounds, though their forms vary across languages.

items.prompt: Who developed the Cherokee syllabary?
items.explanation: Sequoyah created the Cherokee writing system in the early nineteenth century.

items.prompt: ASL is a natural language with ___.
options: English words merely spelled in the air
items.explanation: ASL's grammar differs from English; fingerspelling is only one part of its use.

items.prompt: German speakers may choose 'du' or 'Sie' for one person. What can that choice signal?
items.explanation: The choice reflects social relationships and context, not just singular versus plural.

items.prompt: How was a blend such as 'brunch' formed?
options: By adding a past-tense ending to lunch
By combining parts of breakfast and lunch
items.explanation: Blends fuse parts of existing words to make a new word.

items.prompt: In an abugida such as Devanagari, what does a basic consonant sign normally include?
items.explanation: Vowel signs or a vowel-cancelling mark modify the consonant's default vowel.

items.prompt: In an invented language, 'pa' means fish and 'ba' means tree. What does this pair establish?
options: /p/ and /b/ must be the same phoneme
items.explanation: Same environment, one changed sound, different meaning: this is a minimal pair.

items.prompt: Which language commonly places the verb after both subject and object?
items.explanation: Japanese has a dominant subject–object–verb order; English is normally subject–verb–object.

items.prompt: Why can an Arabic letter look different depending on where it sits in a word?
options: Each position is a different language
items.explanation: Many Arabic letters have different contextual shapes according to how they join.

items.prompt: Adding '-ness' to 'kind' creates ___.
options: A plural form of the same adjective
items.explanation: Kindness is a derived word, not an inflected plural of kind.

items.prompt: Someone says 'Mina has stopped cycling.' What does that normally take for granted?
items.explanation: Stopped triggers a presupposition that the earlier activity occurred.

items.prompt: Basque is traditionally spoken on both sides of the border between ___.
items.explanation: The Basque language area spans parts of northern Spain and southwestern France.

items.prompt: Hiragana and katakana are both used to write which language?
items.explanation: Japanese writing combines kana with kanji, among other elements.

items.prompt: An ending tells the listener 'I heard this, rather than saw it.' What does it mark?
items.explanation: Grammatical evidentiality marks the evidence or information source for a statement.

items.prompt: Two pronunciations of one phoneme occur in predictable contexts. What are these variants called?
items.explanation: Allophones are different sound realisations treated as one phoneme in a language.

items.prompt: A word meaning 'inside' comes after its noun phrase: 'the box inside'. It is a ___.
items.explanation: The labels distinguish placement after versus before the noun phrase.

items.prompt: Invented words: 'dak' = house, 'dakim' = houses, 'fal' = river. Following the same pattern, 'rivers' is ___.
items.explanation: The examples add the plural suffix -im after the root, so fal becomes falim.

items.prompt: A sign language's grammar must copy the majority spoken language's grammar. Accurate?
items.explanation: Signed languages have independent grammatical systems.

items.prompt: Must every grammatical gender system be based on male versus female?
items.explanation: Some systems classify nouns using distinctions other than sex.

items.prompt: The Vai syllabary developed in which region?
items.explanation: Vai writing developed in the nineteenth century and is used in Liberia and Sierra Leone.

items.prompt: English uses 'went' as the past of 'go', with a different stem. What is this pattern called?
items.explanation: Suppletion uses a different stem within a grammatical paradigm rather than a regular affix alone.

items.prompt: A consonant described as a 'voiceless bilabial stop' is the sound ___.
items.explanation: /p/ is made with a lip closure and no vocal-fold vibration; /m/ is a voiced nasal.

items.prompt: In 'The window was broken by Jo', what is the grammatical subject?
items.explanation: In the passive clause, the affected thing is the subject; Jo is the agent.

items.prompt: Which pair belongs to the Uralic family?
items.explanation: Estonian and Hungarian are both Uralic, though they are not close varieties of one language.

items.prompt: Most Cherokee syllabary characters represent what kind of unit?
items.explanation: A syllabary represents syllables rather than just individual consonants and vowels.

items.prompt: A toy language says 'Nia bread eats' for 'Nia eats bread'. Keeping that order, 'Sol sees Nia' becomes ___.
items.explanation: The given pattern is subject–object–verb, so the object Nia comes before sees.

items.prompt: In Devanagari, what is a virama used to do?
items.explanation: A virama cancels the vowel normally associated with a consonant sign.

items.prompt: A noun takes a special counting word alongside a numeral. What feature may you be seeing?
items.explanation: Numeral classifiers occur in counting constructions and can reflect classes of nouns.

items.prompt: Can two sounds be separate phonemes in one language but variants of one phoneme in another?
items.explanation: Phoneme categories depend on a language's contrasts, not just acoustic differences.

items.prompt: To interpret the location meant by 'here', you normally need ___.
items.explanation: Here is deictic: its reference depends on the context in which it is used.

items.prompt: The Bamum syllabary developed in what is now which country?
items.explanation: The Bamum writing tradition developed in western Cameroon around the turn of the twentieth century.

items.prompt: A toy language forms 'hunter' from 'hunt' by adding 'ka-' at the start. How would it form 'singer' from 'sing'?
items.explanation: The stated derivational rule uses a prefix, so ka- goes before sing.

items.prompt: In a neutral Irish clause, the verb commonly comes ___.
items.explanation: Irish is a well-known example of dominant verb–subject–object order.

items.prompt: Some languages use a person's title instead of a 'you' pronoun in polite speech. What can this achieve?
items.explanation: Avoiding a second-person pronoun can itself be a politeness strategy.

items.prompt: Hangul's syllable blocks are built from letters. Which description fits that structure?
options: A pure logographic system with no letters
An alphabet arranged in syllable blocks
items.explanation: Hangul letters represent sound units even though their layout groups them into syllables.

items.prompt: A toy language turns 'malo' into 'mamalo' by copying its first syllable. Applying that rule to 'pitu' gives ___.
items.explanation: The rule copies only the initial syllable pi, not the whole word.

items.prompt: Ava says 'I won' and Bo says 'I won'. Do their two uses of 'I' refer to the same person?
items.explanation: I refers to the speaker of each utterance, so changing speakers changes the reference.

items.prompt: The initial sound in English 'top' is made mainly with which contact?
options: The tongue at the ridge behind the upper teeth
The lower lip against the upper teeth
items.explanation: /t/ is alveolar; the second description is the place used for sounds such as /f/.

items.prompt: Unicode encodes Braille dot patterns. Does each pattern have one universal letter meaning across all languages?
items.explanation: Unicode represents the dot pattern; language-specific Braille standards determine its meaning.

items.prompt: A speaker tells you 'We won', using an explicitly exclusive 'we'. Are you included in that 'we'?
items.explanation: Exclusive we includes the speaker and others but excludes the addressee.

items.prompt: A toy language has 'lom' = book, 'lomta' = books, 'ner' = star. With the same plural rule, 'nerta' means ___.
items.explanation: The observed -ta ending marks plural; nothing in the data makes it an occupation suffix.

items.prompt: A toy language adds 'na' after a statement to turn it into a yes/no question. What is 'na' doing?
items.explanation: A polar question particle marks a yes/no question; languages place such particles in different positions.

items.prompt: The Ethiopic script is often described as an abugida. What changes in its related character forms?
items.explanation: Related Ethiopic signs encode consonants with different vowels.

items.prompt: Why don't English's French borrowings make it a Romance language?
options: A language's family is chosen by its alphabet
items.explanation: English developed from Germanic varieties; borrowed vocabulary does not replace that ancestry.

items.prompt: How does lexical tone differ from ordinary sentence intonation?
options: It requires shouting instead of speaking
It can distinguish words on the same syllable
items.explanation: Tone can distinguish lexical meaning; intonation also conveys information across phrases.

items.prompt: In 'snowballs', which analysis fits the parts?
items.explanation: Snow and ball form a compound; -s marks its plural.

items.prompt: A toy language uses 'zun' for three and 'zunri' for third. If 'pel' means four and the rule stays the same, fourth is ___.
items.explanation: The ordinal is formed by the suffix -ri, following the given pattern.

items.prompt: Compare 'Kai stopped painting' and 'Kai didn't stop painting'. Which background idea normally survives in both?
items.explanation: The presupposition associated with stopped usually survives negation.

items.prompt: Canadian Aboriginal Syllabics are used for only one language. Is that correct?
items.explanation: Related syllabic systems serve several languages, including Cree and Inuktitut.

items.prompt: Why is 'go → went' not a straightforward example of adding a suffix?
options: The stem changes to a different form
items.explanation: Suppletion replaces the stem within the paradigm rather than applying a regular ending alone.

items.prompt: Two similar sounds never overlap in context and their occurrence is predictable. This is evidence for ___.
options: A minimal pair in the same context
items.explanation: Predictable complementary distribution can support analysing sounds as allophones; it is not itself a minimal pair.

items.prompt: Calling Basque an isolate means ___.
options: No family relationship has been established
items.explanation: An isolate is a language without an established genealogical link to other languages, not one without contact.

items.prompt: In 'The trophy was lifted by Lea', who performs the lifting?
items.explanation: The passive changes grammatical organisation; Lea is still the agent of the action.

items.prompt: To demonstrate a sound contrast with a minimal pair, what must differ between two words?
options: One sound in the same position
items.explanation: The words must differ in meaning and just one sound at the same position.

items.prompt: An evidential ending says a claim was reported by someone else. Does that necessarily mean the speaker is certain it is true?
items.explanation: Information source and confidence are different dimensions; evidentiality marks the former.

items.prompt: Black-and-white photo. Both hands up. ABSOLUTE CINEMA. Which director is in the original image?
items.explanation: That is Martin Scorsese. The reaction photo now reviews everything from films to last-minute goals.

items.prompt: Pop Cat opens its mouth. Which shape turns this ordinary cat into a sound effect?
items.explanation: The open-mouth image gives the cat an enormous O-shaped mouth. Two pictures do most of the work.

items.prompt: Maxwell the Cat has entered the timeline. In the familiar music edits, what does the 3D cat do?
items.explanation: The black-and-white cat spins to music. Keyboard Cat is a different internet employee.

items.prompt: Corporate needs you to find the difference between these two pictures. Pam reports back:
items.explanation: Pam gives Creed identical pictures in The Office. The internet uses the scene to say two supposedly different things are effectively the same.

items.prompt: An astronaut makes a shocking discovery. The astronaut behind him replies...
items.explanation: The second astronaut already knows. The format turns a discovery into a very suspicious secret.

items.prompt: Brr Brr Patapim stomps out of the forest. Which combination are you looking at?
items.explanation: Patapim mixes a monkey-like face with a forest body and huge feet. The crocodile-plane is Bombardiro Crocodilo.

items.prompt: The aura-farming boat kid looks impossibly relaxed. What is he doing while the team rows?
options: Dancing at the front of the boat
items.explanation: The clips show a child posing and dancing on the bow while the crew rows. His stage is moving.

items.prompt: A guy taps his temple. The caption presents a terrible decision as a genius loophole. Which format is this?
items.explanation: Roll Safe pairs the knowing grin and temple tap with deliberately flawed reasoning. Looking clever is doing a lot of work.

items.prompt: You guessed one answer and it was right. Tiny victory, clenched baby fist. Which meme fits?
items.explanation: Success Kid became a go-to image for things going better than expected. Even extremely small wins qualify.

items.prompt: You win a free meal, then drop it on the way out. Which old-school meme specializes in this kind of luck?
items.explanation: Bad Luck Brian captions turn ordinary situations into humiliating or unfortunate outcomes. A win rarely stays a win.

items.prompt: Was the original ABSOLUTE CINEMA image a frame from a Scorsese movie?
options: No, it was a photograph accompanying an interview
Yes, he was acting in one of his films
items.explanation: The photo accompanied a New York Times interview with Scorsese. The caption was added by meme makers.

items.prompt: Your friend insists Pop Cat really opens its mouth that wide. How was the familiar open-mouth image made?
options: It is an unedited frame of the cat yawning
items.explanation: The meme alternates a photo with an edited open-mouth version. The real cat is named Oatmeal.

items.prompt: What surprise was announced in the original Side Eyeing Chloe video?
options: A surprise visit to the dentist
items.explanation: The family announced Disneyland. Chloe’s older sister cried with joy; Chloe supplied the reaction face.

items.prompt: Before Success Kid became the face of winning, where was that photo taken?
items.explanation: Photographer Laney Griner took the picture of her young son Sammy at the beach. The victory captions came later.

items.prompt: The Bad Luck Brian portrait looks like a painfully accurate costume. What was the original picture?
options: A still from a teen comedy
items.explanation: It was a yearbook photograph of Kyle Craven. A friend turned the picture into the meme.

items.prompt: The temple-tapping Roll Safe clip looks like street wisdom. What was it filmed for?
items.explanation: Actor Kayode Ewumi was playing Reece Simpson in Hood Documentary. The confident character became a template for bad logic.

items.prompt: Roll Safe is a character. Which name belongs to the character, rather than the actor?
items.explanation: Kayode Ewumi plays Reece Simpson, also called Roll Safe. Actor and character are two different names.

items.prompt: Before Maxwell spun across everyone’s feed, the 3D cat model was added to which game’s mod scene?
items.explanation: The model was added to Steam Workshop for Garry’s Mod and other Source games. The spinning edits followed.

items.prompt: Maxwell is the meme name. What is the real black-and-white cat’s name?
items.explanation: The cat behind Maxwell is Jess. Uni is another black-and-white cat who has been confused with her.

items.prompt: In Brr Brr Patapim’s original narrated story, who is Slim, the unwanted hat guest?
items.explanation: Slim is the blue frog in the hat. Yes, the monkey-tree creature comes with a hat problem and supporting cast.

items.prompt: Patapim needs help getting Slim out of his hat. The wizard he visits is called...
items.explanation: The narration sends Patapim to a wizard named Tiramisu, who recommends a balloon. Dessert names are doing plot work.

items.prompt: The aura-farming boat clips come from a real Indonesian sporting tradition. Which one?
items.explanation: Pacu Jalur is the boat race. Sepak takraw is a different sport; the viral dancing did not happen at a kick-volleyball match.

items.prompt: Chloe gives the camera that look while her older sister cries. Why is her sister crying in the original video?
options: She is happy about the surprise trip
She is scared of the car ride
items.explanation: Lily cries with joy after hearing about Disneyland. The doubtful reaction belongs to Chloe, not her sister.

items.prompt: In the original Office scene, who is Pam fooling with the identical pictures?
items.explanation: Pam gives the task to acting manager Creed. The meme usually cuts out the person being pranked.
